name: Hikaru Utada
label: Epic Records Japan
lede: At thirteen she cut an R&B record that went nowhere. At sixteen she made the best-selling album in Japanese history. Then she took on America, walked away, and came back with songs about her mother and a video game.

eras.title: A record man's kid in Manhattan
eras.text: Born in New York to a producer and an enka singer, she is writing songs by ten and recording a first album at thirteen. Nobody in Japan hears any of it for years.

years.h: Hikaru Utada is born in New York, to a producer and an enka singer
years.p: Father Teruzane Utada produces records; mother [[Keiko Fuji|3d5ebe93-dfa1-434f-807f-ddab40247c4b]] sings enka. Utada grows up on the Upper East Side and moves to Tokyo at eleven.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Utada starts writing music and lyrics around age ten and later attends Seisen International School and the American School in Japan. Father and daughter co-produce every Japanese album through Fantôme.

years.h: A thirteen-year-old cuts an R&B album at Sony Music Studios
years.p: As Cubic U, Utada records the future Precious in New York over August 5-20, with Teruzane Utada, Keiko Fuji and Booker T. Jones among the producers.
years.xp: Cubic U is both the stage name and the name of the R&B backing band, according to Wikipedia. The same source puts a limited single, "I'll Be Stronger", in 1996 too. Nothing here reaches a wide audience.

eras.title: The flop, then the record that reset Japan
eras.text: Precious misses the charts under the name Cubic U. The Japanese-language debut that follows becomes the best-selling album in the country's history.

years.h: Cubic U's Precious covers the Carpenters and misses the charts
years.p: The English-language debut comes out January 28 on Toshiba EMI. It fails to chart and is never commercially distributed in the US.
years.xp: Lead single "Close to You" is the Burt Bacharach and Hal David song the Carpenters made famous. After First Love, Precious is reissued on March 31, 1999 and reaches No. 2 on the Oricon weekly albums chart with 702,060 copies, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Automatic" and "Time Will Tell" arrive together, three months before First Love
years.p: Utada's first Japanese-language single comes out as a double and sets up the album.

years.h: A sixteen-year-old sells 2,026,870 copies of First Love in one week
years.p: Recorded on weekends around school in New York, Los Angeles and Tokyo, it becomes the best-selling album in Japanese history.
years.xp:
Wikipedia cites 8.7 million copies in Japan and about 18 million worldwide, and says it is the only album certified octuple million by the RIAJ. Utada described the ingredients as a computer, an MD player, time, a desire to express and a deadline. Ted Jensen mixed it at Sterling Sound in New York.

It sits at No. 99 on Rolling Stone Japan's 2007 list of the 100 greatest Japanese rock albums. A 15th anniversary edition in 2014 was capped at 10,000 copies after starting at 5,000.

years.h: In Taiwan, "First Love" is the No. 1 song of the year
years.p: Wikipedia reports 500,000 copies of the album there, the best seller by a Japanese act, and a marching-song slot at the 2000 national high school baseball tournament.

eras.title: Three million-sellers and a video game
eras.text: Distance and Deep River extend a run no other Japanese act had matched, and a game director asks for her by name.

years.h: Same day as Ayumi Hamasaki's A Best, Distance sells 3,002,720 in a week
years.p: A Best debuts at No. 2. Utada and Hamasaki both said the rivalry was a label creation.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the matchup a "label-sponsored campaign", with both singers frustrated by it. Distance was made with American producers including Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis and Rodney Jerkins, and runs R&B through jazz, hip-hop and rock. It goes on to sell over 4.4 million in Japan per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Blow My Whistle" puts Utada with Foxy Brown, Pharrell and Chad Hugo
years.p: The Rush Hour 2 soundtrack single reaches No. 11 on the Billboard 200 and tops the soundtracks chart, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Tetsuya Nomura asks for Utada, and "Hikari" opens Kingdom Hearts
years.p: The English version, "Simple and Clean", plays in the international game. The Japanese single debuts at No. 1 on Oricon.
years.xp:
Nomura said he was "absolutely thrilled when she agreed". "Hikari" sold 270,370 copies in its first week and was No. 10 for the year. In 2008 Guinness World Records listed it as the best-selling video game single in Japan, per Wikipedia.

Utada re-recorded both versions in 2024 with [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]].

years.h: Deep River is the third straight album past three million
years.p: Wikipedia says no other Japanese singer or group had managed three in a row. First week: 2.35 million.
years.xp: The singles were "Traveling", "Hikari" and "Sakura Drops/Letters". Wikipedia lists it as the eighth best-selling album in Japanese history, with over 3.6 million sold.

years.h: Utada marries film director Kazuaki Kiriya
years.p: Kiriya directs the "Passion" video and the film Casshern, which gets an Utada theme in 2004. They divorce in March 2007.

eras.title: Utada takes on America
eras.text: Exodus and This Is the One go out as Utada on Island labels, with Timbaland and Stargate producing. Japan buys them. The US mostly doesn't.

years.cap: Utada on a staircase at Kanto, 2004
years.h: Exodus peaks at No. 160 in the US, with Timbaland on board
years.p: "Devil Inside" tops the US dance club chart. The album sells over a million in Japan and about 55,000 in the US, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Released in Japan September 8 and North America October 5, 2004, on Island Def Jam. "Easy Breezy" did not chart. AllMusic heard "urbane, modern, and avant-garde electronica"; other critics split on the lyrics and on the bid for a Western market.

years.cap: Utada's four outfits on the Utada United 2006 tour
years.h: Utada calls "Hikari" the dawn and "Passion" the dusk
years.p: "Passion" and its English version "Sanctuary" carry Kingdom Hearts II. The single peaks at No. 4 with 49,242 first-week copies.
years.xp: "Passion" is the fourth single from Ultra Blue (June 2006). Recorded at Westlake in California and Bunkamura in Tokyo, per Wikipedia, with a video by Kiriya. Wikipedia reports about 350,000 sold.

years.h: Two million downloads, no physical release: "Flavor of Life"
years.p: The ballad version, from the drama Hana Yori Dango 2, is the first single to do it, per Wikipedia. EMI put it over 7.7 million by July.
years.xp: The drama's producers asked for something like "First Love". Three versions exist: the synth-pop original, the ballad and the CD-only "antidote mix".

years.h: "Beautiful World" opens Utada's four-film Evangelion run
years.p: It is the theme for Evangelion 1.0, the first of four Rebuild films she writes for. The video never shows the singer.

years.cap: Utada at the This Is the One listening party, Sephora, Hollywood, March 2009
years.h: Utada works the Sephora circuit for This Is the One, and the US gives No. 69
years.p: Stargate and Tricky Stewart produce. Utada leaves Island afterward and drops the Utada name.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists about 300,000 sold worldwide and a US promotional run of radio tours, Sephora listening parties and TV spots on KTLA and The Early Show. AllMusic's David Jeffries praised the polish but called most lyrics clichéd; the Japan Times' Daniel Robson called it "bland, accessible and predictable".

eras.title: Six years, and a death
eras.text: She announces a break in 2010, streams a farewell concert, reappears on YouTube in 2012, and loses her mother in 2013.

years.big: "I don't know if it will be 2 years or 5 years."
years.h: Utada steps away from music and won't say for how long
years.p: A blog post on August 9 says the focus since age fifteen has narrowed her life, and promises new music first.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Utada cited wanting a broader range of experiences after devoting ages 15 to 27 to music. Single Collection Vol. 2 followed on November 24, 2010, with five new tracks, and landed at No. 1 with 231,000 first week.

years.h: Two Yokohama Arena nights stream live, and Ustream sets a record
years.p: Wild Life, December 8-9, draws 345,000 unique viewers, per Wikipedia, plus a Ustream record for simultaneous viewers.

years.h: "Sakura Nagashi" breaks the quiet, on YouTube first
years.p: Written after the March 2011 Tohoku earthquake for Evangelion 3.0 with Paul Carter, with a video by Naomi Kawase. It peaks at No. 2 on Billboard Japan.

years.big: "I am proud to be the daughter of my mother."
years.h: Utada's mother, the enka singer Keiko Fuji, dies
years.p: Japan Today reported an apparent suicide. Utada wrote publicly about her days later.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the death to August 22, 2013. In a statement Japan Today dated August 26, Utada said the way her mother ended her life was "beyond sad" and that she remembered only her laughing. Wikipedia ties the themes of Fantôme to this loss.

eras.title: Fantôme, then Epic
eras.text: The comeback album comes out of grief. Then a move to Sony's Epic, a Kingdom Hearts III song with Skrillex, and the A. G. Cook collaboration that sets up Bad Mode.

years.h: Fantôme brings Utada back, with her mother's death behind it
years.p: [[Sheena Ringo|9e414497-23b7-4ab7-9ec6-8ea9864c9e87]] duets, KOHH guests, and the album spends four weeks at No. 1 in Japan.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Sheena Ringo on "Nijikan Dake no Vacance" and KOHH on "Bōkyaku". It debuts at 252,581 copies, wins Album of the Year at the Japan Record Awards and is certified three-times platinum. All three singles were digital-only.

years.h: Utada leaves EMI for Sony's Epic label
years.p: The March 2017 move ends nearly two decades on Toshiba EMI and its successors. The back catalogue reaches streaming in January 2018.

years.h: Hatsukoi, her first album for Epic, enters at No. 1
years.p: It tops Oricon's physical and digital charts, with over 242,000 sold per Wikipedia.
years.xp: "Hatsukoi" is the title of the album and of a single released May 30, 2018. Utada had by then divorced a second spouse; Wikipedia gives April 2018.

years.cap: Utada on the Laughter in the Dark Tour, 2018
years.h: Skrillex gets a remix request and answers with "Face My Fears"
years.p: Utada asks him to remix "Chikai". He proposes a new song instead. With Poo Bear, it becomes her first Billboard Hot 100 entry, at No. 98.
years.xp: "Chikai" ("Don't Think Twice" in English) is the Kingdom Hearts III ending theme. Wikipedia calls "Face My Fears" Utada's first original English song since This Is the One and says it reached No. 9 on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs. The CD single followed January 18, 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: One Last Kiss (Hikaru Utada song)
years.h: Hideaki Anno directs "One Last Kiss", and Evangelion ends
years.p: Utada asks Anno to make the video. A. G. Cook co-produces.
years.xp: It reaches No. 1 on Billboard Japan's Hot 100 and Oricon's combined chart, per Wikipedia, and No. 40 on Billboard's Global 200. Utada said the film is about loss and grief.

years.h: Utada comes out as nonbinary on an Instagram livestream
years.p: She uses she/her and they/them, per Wikipedia, and says Ms. and Mrs. never fit.

eras.title: Bad Mode, and a look back
eras.text: A bilingual album made across the pandemic with PC Music and Floating Points in the room, then a twenty-fifth anniversary.

years.h: Pitchfork gives Bad Mode 8.0 and ranks it No. 31 of 2022
years.p: Utada co-produces with [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]], [[Floating Points|69d9c5ba-7bba-4cb7-ab32-8ccc48ad4f97]], Skrillex and Poo Bear, and sings in both Japanese and English.
years.xp:
Joshua Minsoo Kim wrote the Pitchfork review, per Wikipedia. Slant ranked it No. 9 of 2022; Gorilla vs. Bear put it at No. 19. It topped Oricon and Billboard Japan, finished No. 26 on Oricon's year-end chart and went Gold from the RIAJ with 166,698 certified units.

Recorded between 2018 and 2021; the physical release followed on February 23, 2022. The Japan Times called it "a career highlight".

years.h: Live Sessions from Air Studios goes to Netflix
years.p: A studio concert film of Utada's songs.

years.cap: Utada on the Science Fiction Tour at Saitama Super Arena, July 24, 2024
years.h: Science Fiction marks twenty-five years, and a tour follows
years.p: Utada announces the best-of on December 9. A tour of Japan, Taiwan and Hong Kong runs through 2024.

sources.title: Wikipedia: One Last Kiss (Hikaru Utada song)
